reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported. I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 260, 263, 265 with the same amounts). Next I need the customer list, so I'll fetch the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly. The orders show three customers, acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get acme's net balance first.
Acme's net balance came back as 29089. Next I'll get birch's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
Acme (29089) and birch (62075) have their net balances. Cobalt is the last customer in the orders list, so I'll fetch its net balance before recording any payouts.

The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the net balances agree with the order totals minus refunds (acme 46365-17276=29089, birch 62075, cobalt 50341-10903=39438). I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout of 29089 recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 62075 matches its orders (32750 + 29325, no refunds), so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net balance is 39438, which matches its orders (33488 + 16853 = 50341) minus its refund (10903). The refunds table matched Alpha's report, so I'll record cobalt's payout now.

All three payouts recorded successfully. I checked each against the orders and refunds: acme 46365 - 17276 = 29089, birch 62075 with no refunds, and cobalt 50341 - 10903 = 39438. The refunds table matched Alpha's report before any payout.
